question: A can do a certain work in the same time in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together could do it in 10 days and C alone in 50 days, then B alone could do it in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = **LCM**(10, 50) = **50 units**.

Efficiency of (A + B) = 5 units/day and Efficiency of C = 1 unit/day.

Total Efficiency (A + B + C) = 5 + 1 = **6 units/day**.

Given **A = B + C**, so Efficiency of A = 6 ÷ 2 = **3 units/day**.

Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A = 5 − 3 = **2 units/day**.

Time for B = 50 ÷ 2 = **25 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = **10 days**

Time taken by C alone = **50 days**

Condition: Efficiency of **A = Efficiency of (B + C)**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of (A + B + C) = 5 + 1 = **6 units/day**

⇒ Since Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (B + C)

⇒ A + (B + C) = 6 ⇒ A + A = 6

⇒ 2 × Efficiency of A = 6

⇒ Efficiency of A = **3 units/day**

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of B = 5 − 3 = **2 units/day**

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time = 50 ÷ 2 = **25 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. **Efficiency = Work ÷ Time**.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their **total efficiency** is the sum of their individual efficiencies.

Time Calculation

Total time taken to complete the work = **Total Units of Work ÷ Combined Efficiency**.</p
